# Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0504a)

**ID:** Atk S0504a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Commentary on the Itivuttaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*, also known as the *Paramatthadīpanī II* (or *Paramattha-Dīpanī*), is the commentary on the *Itivuttaka* belonging to the Khuddakanikāya commentary collection [Karashima 2012; Dhammadinna 2014]. It is authored by the commentator Ācariya Dhammapāla, who explicitly records in the prologue that his exegesis was composed in strict conformity with the Mahāvihāra tradition [Karashima 2012; Endo 1997]. The work contains an extensive commentary on the opening *nidāna* formula [Almogi 2014], detailed etymological expositions of titles and epithets such as *Bhagavā* and *Tathāgata*, and structured numerical listings of the virtues of the Buddha (*buddha-guṇa*) [Endo 1997]. Its explanations of doctrinal formulas and terms were regarded as authoritative in the Theravāda commentarial tradition; for example, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* refers readers directly to both the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* for unabridged treatments of the epithet *Tathāgata* [Endo 1997].

The text was critically edited for the Pali Text Society by M. M. Bose in two volumes, with indexes prepared by Hermann Kopp [Karashima 2012; Endo 1997; Langer 2007].

**Sources**

- [Karashima 2012] Seishi Karashima, Abhisamācārikā Dharmāḥ (2012) — Supplies the alternative title Paramatthadīpanī II, Dhammapāla's authorship, and translation bibliographical details.
- [Almogi 2014] Orna Almogi, ed., Evolution of Scriptures, Formation of Canons: The Buddhist Case (2014) — Notes the extensive commentary on the nidāna in the text and records an Indian edition by Mithilesh Prasad.
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Discusses Dhammapāla's Mahāvihāra allegiance in the prologue, exegeses of Bhagavā and Tathāgata, buddha-guṇa lists, cross-references from the Theragāthā commentary, and PTS edition details.
- [Dhammadinna 2014] Dhammadinna, ed., Research on the Dīrgha-āgama (2014) — Identifies the text as Paramatthadīpanī (II) authored by Dhammapāla.
- [Langer 2007] Rita Langer, Buddhist Rituals of Death and Rebirth: Contemporary Sri Lankan Practice (2007) — Confirms the PTS edition by M. M. Bose.
